lines.english: "Ooh, it finally looks like a place suitable for living."
After coming home from practice, and whilst taking off her disguise, Kazusa stares at her transformed room in surprise.
"…You look rather proud for someone who didn't do anything."
Of course she'd be surprised.
After all, I did a thorough cleaning of this place, changed the curtains, put the furniture together and set up all electronic devices for her, all by myself…
"It's your job to watch over me, Haruki. You earned the right to do coverage of me on that condition… I haven't done anything unreasonable, you know?"
"Then let me interview you right away."
"Let's have dinner first. I'm hungry. What's the matter? Is dinner still not ready?"
T-This woman…
"…I've been cleaning up the place up until now. I'll start making dinner now. By the way, I do happen to be really exhausted."
"I see. Then wake me when it's done. Ah… I can finally sleep in a bed."
T-This woman…
I thought of asking her whether she had the decency to offer help, but I gave up right before the words left my mouth.
I'd only have more to deal with if she does end up helping me. In a way, Kazusa's choice is indeed the right one.
"I don't have the time to make anything proper, so we'll have instant food, okay?"
"That sounds good. I'll actually be able to have some decent food for once."
…That explanation doesn't satisfy me one bit, though.
"Hey, look here."
"I said stop. Don't take pictures of people eating."
"Don't hide your face…"
When we finished our store-bought Chinese meat bowl, Kazusa opened the convenience store cake as if it was the true meal of the evening.
But when I tried taking pictures of that particular scene, she refused by blocking the lens of my camera with her hands.
"You're acting like a paparazzi. This is the height of a peeping fetish."
"I think that your sweets addiction might make for a good article, though."
I don't deny her accusation, because even I agree.
When I see that happy face Kazusa makes when she's eating these cheap cakes, I can't resist the urge to immortalize it in a photo.
"Is seeing me eat a cake that much of an oddity?"
"It doesn't suit your image. After all, you have a 'primarily black and stylish get-up.'"
"…Don't say it like that. It irritates me."
By the way, what just fell into her mouth is a primarily white and cute strawberry shortcake.
It's a two-pack worth 300 yen, but it goes without saying that I don't get a share. …Though it's not like I want any.
"Hey, you got your love of sweets from your mother, didn't you?"
"At first I didn't realize…"
"Hmm…"
I turn on the voice recorder, and put it on the table.
Kazusa frowns at it a little, but according to our "contract," she continues talking.
"Ever since I was a kid, every time I ate dinner with mom, there'd always be a vast variety of desserts."
"Cakes, pudding, donuts… Mostly western sweets. It wasn't 'cake today, pudding tomorrow.' All of them were lined up on the table at the same time."
"…Guh."
"It was our habit back when I was a kid to drink coffee with plenty of sugar and milk…"
"Didn't you ever find it gross?"
"No, it's delicious, is it not?"
"…There should be a limit."
"She was able to eat it all without a care… That's how much strength and willpower she must've had."
"I see…"
Even after eating that much sugar, she played concerts intense enough to use it all up.
And she ended up passing down that rare type of metabolism to her daughter, along with the skill she molded from the energy obtained by that disposition.
"The first time someone told me that was weird was during a school trip in elementary school. During a group activity, we went to a candy shop in Kyoto…"
"Oh, so you participated in events like that back then."
"The parents of my classmates said all kinds of things back then. I lost count of how many times they asked about my father's name. As if I'd know."
"Well, they weren't many but I did have friends. They didn't bully me that much."
"That sounds nice… somewhat."
"I didn't mind what others said about me… but only as long as they weren't someone close to me."
"But that was a misunderstanding, though."
"Don't come up with explanations when you're only supposed to listen. Your job is to write what I tell you, isn't it?"
"Then I'll write what you just said. Is that okay?"
"It's fine, but is this even interesting to hear?"
"That's for me, my superior, and the readers to decide. For the time being, you can just focus on talking about yourself."
"Hmm… I don't really get it, but can you even put something like this in a for-profit magazine?"
"The cake-addicted pianist?"
"What a strange…
Ah."
"Yeah… Thank you for that."
"Stop it… it's embarrassing."
Despite the sound of the shutter, Kazusa still puts the fork in her mouth, softly forgiving me with an embarrassed look.
"Yeah, that expression looked really natural. Want to take a look?"
"Of course I don't. Damn it, I've been had."
That expression tells me everything I need to know. The happiness Kazusa gets when she eats sweet foods causes her heart to temporarily soften.
"Is that so? I think it's a good image. There's even a bit of cream stuck on the corner of your mouth…"
"Delete it! Delete it so no trace remains of it!"
"Come on. The early bird gets the worm, right?"
"…I'm cold."
It's 8 AM, Thursday.
After I had woken up at my usual time and made the usual breakfast, I went over to Kazusa's apartment only to see her spectacularly glued to the bed…
No matter how many times I gave her a shake, she only responded with "I don't need breakfast" or "Let me sleep a little longer." Thus, I had to exact divine punishment on her like this.
I forced her to change her clothes, bound her hair, and forced her out of the apartment without further setbacks, taking her out with me on our morning walk.
"Oh, it's starting to get frosty. Of course it's cold."
I knew that the morning temperature was going to be 1°C below freezing point…
"Why am I in a place like this…?"
After we left the apartment we went to Minami-Suetsugu Station, walked past the front gate of Houjou University and Houjou High School, and now we're strolling along the river.
This path is rarely used by the students commuting by train, so it's less crowded than the area around our apartment, making it ideal for our walk.
The river is beautiful for being something inside a metropolis. There's even a lot of vegetation. That's precisely why the cold permeates this area that much more…
"Ah, hey! I was going to step on that!"
"You stepped on all the ones on the other side, so what's the big deal?"
"I saved this one for last. I got the feeling this one might make the best sound."
"Ah, half of my heel is sunk in. This is pretty fun…"
"I know that it's fun. That's precisely why…"
"Crunch, crunch…"
"Aah, stop, stop it…"
To distract themselves from the cold, two fully grown adults destroy one patch of frost after another…
Two schoolgirls pass those two immature adults with somewhat awkward expressions on their faces.
A few seconds after that encounter…
Kazusa stares at those two girls with a complex expression for a while.
"You used to wear the same uniform as them once."
"You too, Haruki…"
"Unfortunately, my uniform wasn't so short around the knee."
"…Either point out the idiocy of what I said or make fun of me. There's no backing out of that statement."
"Don't worry, I wasn't listening."
Even while calmly responding to me in that manner, Kazusa's eyes are still firmly aimed at those girls.
No, more accurately…
"Do you feel nostalgic?"
She might be seeing ourselves in them.
"You wore that too during high school."
"What about it?"
"If you're going to answer so stubbornly, you can stop staring at them like that."
That might have been a harsh comeback.
"I don't feel nostalgia at all. I'm not allowed to feel it."
Even at my uncalled for comment, Kazusa doesn't avert her eyes from those girls.
"What's that supposed to mean?"
"The night after I came back to Japan, Haruki, I told you, didn't I?"
"…Told me what?"
"I'll never come back here again."
"I won't ever come near any place that I used to know… or any place that has a history with me."
"That was a mere two weeks ago…"
I asked Kazusa a question, yet she continued as if I understood everything.
…Not that I don't understand, though.
"I'm so weak-willed. I'm so indecisive. Am I an idiot or something…?"
"Why can't you come close?"
Left without a choice, I ask her a question with the presumption that she too understands.
But I can't fully accept what she has to say.
I don't want to hear nor acknowledge her self-deprecating words.
"Are you going to ask me that? Are you going to make me say it?"
"You really have cruel taste. It might be the result of your work."
Done with stepping on patches of frost, Kazusa slowly moves down toward the river.
She occasionally trips on the slippery grass, yet she never grabs onto my outstretched hands.
"It's not nostalgic at all."
"Ah…"
The sunlight is reflected by the surface of the river, and shines on Kazusa's face with a swaying motion.
But unlike the radiance of the light, the illuminated expression is covered in grief…
"Kazusa… look at me."
"No."
I can't keep myself from clicking the shutter.
"I told you no… you coward."
"Take off your glasses this time…"
"Don't give me orders."
Kazusa, who called me a "coward," started looking me straight in the eyes at some point.
With the same attitude she used to say "Don't give me orders," she slowly shows me her eyes no longer hidden behind her glasses.
"Your hat, and your scarf too."
"Don't push your luck. Don't ask me to do whatever you want…"
This time, her hidden true face is exposed to me.
Kazusa grimaced from the cold a bit, but after that… she started glaring at my lens.
Maybe it was just my imagination that her lips seemed to be quivering.
"Hey, Kazusa…"
"What is it?"
"Even if you are an idiot…"
"I prefer the Kazusa… who walks down the same road we used to in the past with me."
"…That's why I'm not allowed to get close."
"Take off your hair ornaments too… and become the usual Kazusa again."
Now without any hint of stubbornness, Kazusa releases her hair just as I desire.
Her long black hair flutters in the cold wind, softly blending in with the light coming from the water.
This divine shot is probably not one that can be taken by someone of my skill…
"I knew that it was going to be this fun… I knew I would feel this happy…"
"I knew that if I returned home with these feelings, I'd just make the eventual pain worse…"
"I'll resent you, mom…"
"…Are you still at work? I'm already home, you know? What about dinner?"
"Of course I didn't eat… Weren't you the one who told me to stop dining outside!? You said it was bad for my nutrient intake."
"What did you say? Are you telling me to rinse rice? Do you think I'm capable of something so ambitious?"
"…As long as you understand. 30 minutes. I can't wait any longer than that."
"What will happen if you don't make it in time? Are you planning on starving me to death or something?"
"Huh? Sign autographs? Like I'd do something like that."
"I don't give a crap about that! You say they gave you colored paper for me to sign without asking for permission!?"
"…Ah, I've had enough of your excuses. Just come home quickly. My empty stomach is reaching its limit."
"Oh, and buy pudding on the way home… The one that's sold in large three-packs. You know, the one they sell at the neighborhood supermarket."
"The ones we bought the day before yesterday? Obviously there aren't any left."
"Well then, run with all your might… Do you plan on making me wait even longer?"
"Haah, jeez…"
"Ah…"
"S-Setsu…"
"Sorry for disturbing you."
"Ah…"
"Haah, maybe he's not home after all. What should I do?"
"Ah, crap, it's already time for our meeting…"
"…? Is there something you want?"
"Who are you…?"
"And who are you to ask?"
"Ah, I am that guy's… the neighbor of the person living in that apartment."
"Oh, is that so? Well thank you."
"So, who are you?"
"I'm an acquaintance of your neighbor, what of it?"
"…Is that all?"
"What do you mean?"
"N-No! I don't care at all! After all, I only just moved in!"
"Is that so?"
"Ah, yes. So what business do you have with my neighbor?"
"I thought you didn't care."
"I don't care at all!"
"Truth is, I had something to give him, but it looks like he's out…"
"Yes… he'll be home soon… I think."
"What should I do…? If I put it in the mailbox, he might miss it."
"I-If you have a message for him, I can tell him in your stead."
"Ah… would you be so kind? I'd like you to give this to your neighbor when he comes home."
"A letter…?"
"It's a ticket for a concert tomorrow."
"A concert…?"
"My friend… your neighbor's girlfriend is singing, but she hasn't given him a ticket yet."
"Ah…"
"That's how it is, so can I also ask you to tell him that he absolutely has to attend it?"
"Ah, yes… yeah, I got it. I'll tell him."
"Thank you very much. In that case, I'm counting on you."
"Ah, yes…"
"My neighbor's girlfriend…"
"…It couldn't be."
"There is no way… Could she be…"
"…N-No! I'm a bit prettier than her, right!?"
"What is this…? What does it say?"
"It's meant to be German writing… but I guess it's off the mark?"
"Your writing is usually so precise that it's almost mechanical, yet your cursive writing is completely unreadable."
"Then you go ahead and write for me. A sample is good enough."
"I don't wanna. Go ahead and reap what you sowed. I'll stay right here and watch over you."
"I'll take responsibility for that… but in exchange, don't ever sign an autograph even if someone asks you on the spot. At least during your time in Japan."
"I've always refused them, so don't worry. Come on, Haruki, look this way."
"Shut up. I'm busy."
I'm too busy writing Kazusa's autographs for her…
Friday.
My progress report to Hamada-san ended in less than 30 minutes.
After that, while compiling the work sent to me as miscellaneous work, for some reason there was a mountain of colored paper in front of me.
…It seems that news of my exclusive coverage of Touma Kazusa has spread throughout the entire company.

I thought that it was weird since there are plenty of people who have connections with celebrities through our job, but a certain freelance writer with connections to the celebrity world solved that mystery.
It seems that their response is not only determined on the basis of someone being famous, but also the level of scarcity.
…In other words, the autographs I'm signing right now will probably end up in some internet auction.
"Hey, Haruki."
"No, I won't look at you and I won't smile. It's only fair since you're not doing this yourself."
"It's not about that…"
"Then what is it? There is no more dessert. You need to worry about your nutritional balance after eating…"
"It's about Setsuna."
"It's about Setsuna and you, Haruki… I want you to tell me about the two of you these past five years."
"…Why would you ask that?"
"I just felt like it."
Little by little, Kazusa crosses over the line.
"Though maybe that's being irresponsible… The real reason is that at some point, I'd have to hear about it anyway."
The topic left alone ever since she came to Japan… No, ever since she entered this apartment.
By both Kazusa and me…
"Because I did something terrible to Setsuna."
"No you haven't."
"But Setsuna is…"
"The one who did something terrible to Setsuna is me. It's all my fault."
I have no idea why Kazusa brought this up all of a sudden.
There was no sign of it until this morning.
These past few days we've repeated a lifestyle of Kazusa one-sidedly verbally abusing me, and me one-sidedly lecturing her, with both of us completely ignoring the other.
"Even that is completely solved now. There's nothing for you to feel responsible for, Kazusa."
That's why I'm getting cautious in response to Kazusa's sudden change in demeanor…
"So you're saying that… I have nothing to do with your memories together? That the value of those memories will decrease if you tell me?"
"I never said any such thing…"
But Kazusa doesn't allow me to run away.
Far sharper than during our reunion in France, she aims to pierce myーand her ownーheart.
"Then go ahead and tell me. Tell me that you're sick of me."
"It's okay… I won't feel a thing. No, that's wrong. The more I'll hear, the more nostalgic I'll feel, and the happier I'll be."
From a sense of responsibility, to mere reminiscence…
At some point, Kazusa's reasons for wanting to hear about Setsuna… had changed.
Because of those obvious changes, I understand.
That all her reasons were lies to begin with, and which reason is the true one.
That no matter how much I negate it, Kazusa will never be free from her guilt.
That no matter how much Kazusa accepts us, she'll never be able to hear about Setsuna and me with only happiness in her heart.
…She couldn't, right?
"Then let us start.
Ehm, today I'd like to ask some questions of Kitahara Haruki-san, the hope of Kaiousha. I look forward to working with you."
After these past days of aggressive interviewing from me, Kazusa has completely memorized my methods of interviewing.
Turning off the recorder whenever she says something inappropriate, removing image data that reflects badly on her, and taking countless pictures of the food I made.
"First and foremost, I'd like to ask about your past five years… and the girlfriend who supported you along the way."
"Kazusa…"
And now, in order to not let any of my true feelings slip by, and to expose all my lies, she presses the record button.
"…And that's how I arrived at the present."
"It took three whole years. I hurt Setsuna for three whole years."
Just as Kazusa memorized the methods of the interviewer.
I also managed to memorize the methods of the interviewee.
"Until we were able to face each other again. Until we vowed to overcome what happened back then."
As the interviewer urges me on, I pour my heart out.
But still choosing my words, differentiating the self that I want to show her and the self I want to keep hidden.
"Until Setsuna was able to sing again."
Looking at the empty space instead of her, so she wouldn't be able to catch on to my true feelings.
"Those three years of struggle felt incredibly long."
A speech that is half true, and half nonsensical even to myself. A story that could perhaps be labeled as "non-fiction."
"I desperately tried living a boring everyday life, while Setsuna tried to act unnaturally cheerful while carrying with her all those wounds… That's what she told me later."
Why am I telling her all this? Why does Kazusa want to hear any of this?
In the past, she'd get mad at me for talking about Setsuna.
"That's exactly why… the two years we spent free from our shackles went by in a flash."
That's right… I remember talking about Setsuna with this much passion sometime in the past too.
"The first year was about our graduation, our job hunting, our friends, our family, and Setsuna's singing…"
Setsuna joined the Light Music Club, and we knew that the "pianist in Music Room 2" was Kazusa.
In order to get the third member to join, I sang the praises of the second member.
"The second year was about our jobs, the changes in our environment, the fact that our time together was decreasing compared to our university days, things like that."
I spoke about Setsuna whom I had known for a week to Kazusa whom I had known for half a year with an incredible passion… apparently.
The proof of that is in the fact that Kazusa quickly got angry, and threw me out of the music room along with my chair as I was still talking.
"A lot might have happened… but I felt that we could overcome them together, and we actually did overcome them."
Back then, I had no hesitation when speaking of Setsuna's attractive qualities, and I had no trouble acknowledging Kazusa's strong points.
I was reckless. I was giving both Kazusa and Setsuna "special treatment."
I simply loved both of them. It wasn't an affection where I had to choose one or the other.
"That's why, um… Setsuna and I…"
But now…
"Our feelings won't waver anymore…"
We two cannot be allowed to like each other.
We are far too grown up for me to innocently proclaim that I "like both."
I take a glance at Kazusa's face for the first time in a while, and notice she isn't looking at me anymore at all.
Just like me, she stares at the empty space with an expression that won't let her true feelings be exposed.
She isn't angry over my lengthy speech. Neither does she show any interest, despite hearing exactly what she wanted to hear.
She remains so utterly silent and shows so little interest that I almost want to ask her "then why did you ask?"
"Kazusa…"
"Hm?"
And she gives a vague nod to my call…
"You spoke well… Here, I'll give you this."
She puts a single envelope on the table.
"…What is this?"
"A woman I don't know… gave this to me and told me to give it to my neighbor."
Out of the envelope came a single ticket.
"It's for a concert, apparently. …She said my neighbor's girlfriend is going to sing."
"I see…"
"Also… she told me to tell you that you absolutely have to go."
It must have been Yanagihara Tomo.
Setsuna's self-proclaimed promoter. The underclassman who has become even more meddlesome than before.
…It must be Io's influence. Thanks to her, everyone around me is like that.
"This is a reward for telling me everything… though it's yours to begin with."
I see… She's going to sing.
Setsuna is going to sing again.
She has been on a hiatus ever since she got employed, but ever since that Valentine's Day concert, she has been on stage countless times.
Finding spare time between her job hunting and her graduation thesis, she held positions in numerous bands, always finding an opportunity to sing.
The concerts she appeared in always sold out. Hearing of her reputation, some pretty major bands sent requests to either recruit her or hire her as backup.
But Setsuna never desired any further fame than that. She only sang when she could, with friends who shared the same interest.
It seems that she actually wanted to appear on stage with me. She would quarrel with me sometimes when I refused.
"She said it was going to start at 6 PM tomorrow. Go to her."
No explanation is necessary as to… why she's doing this now.
"Go listen to Setsuna sing with a bouquet in your hands. And hug her while you're there…"
Because Setsuna always sang even in the face of hardship… No, Setsuna always sang because of hardship.
Because ever since that day, she's put her feelings into her songs and overcome everything.
"What's the matter?"
The thing that's causing Setsuna hardship right now…
And the thing I'm doing right now, that might cause her even more hardship is…
1. I'm not going.
2. I can't go.
"Why not? Setsuna is going to sing, you know? Didn't you always love her singing?"
"Don't use past tense… I love it even now."
The answer to her question was so obvious that I almost got a bit moody in my answer.
Because it's obvious that I love all the music played by those close to me.
"Then go. Why are you being so stubborn?"
"I'm in the middle of an important job right now. I'll have to postpone my own plans for a while."
"Does that… mean that it's my fault?"
"…Just kidding. The truth is that Setsuna and I are in the middle of a cold war right now. I promised to not meet her until she contacts me first."
"…What does that mean?"
I avoided Kazusa's question in order to negate her guilt. In exchange, I exposed the circumstances between Setsuna and me.
Even when I tried to hide it, this is the destination I've arrived at due to my poor conversational abilities, and my unstable feelings.
A topic that has no place in our five year long history. Something that happened only recently.
To be precise, it's something that started on Christmas Eve. An accumulation of a small dispute I had with Setsuna.
Because I didn't tell her about Kazusa until we were back home, I ended up breaking our one-week rule.
Now we haven't met for ten whole days. I haven't even heard her voice.
"…So it really was my fault."
"Of course not. It's my fault for not telling her anything."
"But if I hadn't chased you back then… If I hadn't called out to you…"
"Our interview was scheduled before we met. That had nothing to do with it."
"But at least you'd have been able to go to the Christmas Mass with Setsuna. Things wouldn't have gotten so complicated…"
"I was happy… to see you again."
Normally, that would have been nothing but a lie to ease Kazusa's guilt.
…It shouldn't have reflected my true feelings.
"That's why it's not your fault, Kazusa. It's my fault, for never being able to ease Setsuna's mind no matter how much time passes…"
"Then… don't accept this kind of job… Are you an idiot?"
"Shut up…"
She probably knows that people become unreasonably angry when hit with the truth.
"Staying by my side, continuing to grant my selfish wishes… All that will only cause Setsuna more pain, won't it?"
Yet I still couldn't leave you be.
I couldn't stand seeing you suffer. I wanted to help you…
"It's okay. Didn't I tell you earlier? That our feelings would never waver again."
But of course I can't tell her that.
If I tell Kazusa that, she will suffer, and I can't bear to see Kazusa suffer.
Kazusa turns off the recorder.
In other words, the interview is over.
All that is left for her is to gather up the equipment, and bid the interviewee farewell.
It's already past midnight. It has long surpassed the hour where it's appropriate for someone to be in the apartment of a woman living by herself.
"I'm sure Setsuna has become beautiful. She has always been too good for you."
"I can attest to that."
"…Going that far in your flattery of her?"
"It's the truth. You'll see if you meet her."
I do think I'm being a bit excessive in my praise of Setsuna, but even then, those around me used to keep telling me I undervalued Setsuna more than anyone else.
…They told me that if I did value her as much as she's due, I'd be crushed under the degree of my own inferiority.
"Hey, Haruki."
"Hm?"
"Then, I have a request for you…"
"Good evening, we're Routes… I-Incidentally featuring SETSUNA just for tonight."
"Um… I've been inactive for a while. Last time I sang was a year ago… Does anyone remember me?"
"Wah, amazing! Look, look, Leader! Didn't I tell you I'm not old news?"
"…Um, now then, since it seems that it'll take a bit more time for the instruments to be tuned, I'd like for you to listen to me speak a tiny bit."
"Today, I've returned for the first time in a year, and the truth is that a lot has happened during that time."
"To be a bit more precise, in April last year, I gained full-time employment."
"Thank you very much."
"Because of that, I had to focus on my work in order to get used to it. I built up a lot of stress not being able to sing."
"But I thought that perhaps I'll be able to return in my second year… or so I hoped. It actually looks like I'm only going to get more busy from now on."
"Even then, I do feel like I'll get some mental leeway, so I want to continue singing in front of you all every now and then."
"So there you have it. My slightly reserved declaration of my come-back… I look forward to singing for you all in the future."
"Ah, it looks like they're about ready. Well then, enjoy our first song… 'Routes.'"
"Haaaah, it's over…!"
"Good work… You're more tense than the person actually singing as usual, I see."
"But it's been a whole year, you know? A whole year. Ah, that was the best…"
"To think such an overzealous fan would have her sights on her… Poor SETSUNA."
"Hey, hey, are people in the entertainment industry here?"
"I did see a few of them, but I can't find them right away. How about you look for them yourself?"
"You're so cold, Master. I was all over the place advertising the live show today."
"You didn't need to do that. Just by putting SETSUNA in the advertisements is enough to fill the whole venue."
"She's this popular, yet she has no intention of getting somewhere in the industry at all."
"She's a normal girl once she gets off the stage. Not to say that she's not extraordinarily cute."
"Did you find someone from the industry?"
"…It's the neighbor."
"Your neighbor? Then go greet them."
"No, Setsuna's neighbor… actually, more like an acquaintance of an acquaintance."
"Which one is it?"
"That girl with the hat and glasses. Look, the one standing in the far back."
"…A model?"
"…You think so too? Her style, and that face."
"Doesn't it look like she's in disguise? Her getup has an air of wanting to avoid attention."
"I see, that's one way of looking at it… Does that mean she's one of those famous industry people?"
"What's the matter, Master? You look perplexed."
"No… It feels like I've seen her before after all, and recently at that."
"Hmm…?"
"Will you go greet her?"
"No, I'm fine. She might be part of the industry, but she doesn't look like someone here to recruit Setsuna."
"I suppose so. I'd imagine a girl like her is the one being recruited usually."
"If anything, we're supposed to look for people who look like producers. You don't think Ogata Eiji might be here?"
"You have a lot of guts name-dropping such a bigwig."
"But that's how much ability Setsuna has. It's a crime to let her talent go to waste!"
"But if she herself isn't shining with passion, she can't rise in a relentless world like that."
"Even then, Setsuna has something special about her. Something fate-like, unrelated to her own feelings."
"You mean like being zeroed in by an overzealous fan like you?"
"That's not everything. She's been legendary since she debuted. Don't you know about the Houjou High School Festival five years ago?"
"Of course I know. You've told me about it countless times."
"It was an impromptu three-person band, yet people crowded even outside the gymnasium."
"Not to mention that the keyboardist is now a world-famous pianist."
"Yes, yes, Touma Kazusa! Thinking about it now, it's almost like a miracle…?"
"Speaking of Touma Kazusa, she's back in Japan now. Isn't her first Japanese concert next week?"
"She's SETSUNA's friend, so couldn't you pull a few strings to get some tickets?"
"Touma… Kazusa…?"
"What's the matter, Tomo? You look like you've seen a ghost."
"～～～!? A-Ah… Aaaah!?"
"…Tomo?"
"M-Master! Where did that person earlier go? You know, that girl I called the neighbor…"
"Ah, if you're talking about her, she just left."
"N-No way, no way… What, what does that mean…?"
"How was it?"
"Setsuna was there…"
"I suppose so."
"Then, I have a request for you…"
"If you're not going, can you give that ticket to me?"
"I want to see Setsuna. I want to see what Setsuna is like now, if even for a single glance."
With those words, Kazusa went toward the concert hall with her usual disguise…
Once the performance was over and she came out, she looked as if she was on the verge of tears.
Her eyes were pure red, so I'm sure it was actually the aftermath.
"Singing with so much enjoyment like always… That part of her hasn't changed at all."
"Yeah…"
"…Though I shouldn't say that so easily. After all, it took her three years to get it back."
"Hiding in the shadow of Setsuna's dazzling self is her other self that has cried three years' worth of tears."
"Kazusa…"
"When I thought about that… Um, I was happy to see Setsuna smile, but my chest started to hurt."
Kazusa turns her back to me, and her voice changes into one heaving with sobs.
I'm sure she doesn't want to let me see her expression, nor let me hear her voice.
"Let's go home, Haruki… I'm sorry for making you pick me up."
"Aren't you… going to meet Setsuna?"
"That's impossible."
"Should I call her? She should still be in the dressing room…"
"No, stop it."
"Why…?"
"If you do that, then you won't be able to come up with any excuses. She'll find out we're meeting each other just by knowing I was at the concert."
"But we haven't done anything…"
"It doesn't matter what happened. Even if it was nothing more than an interview, Setsuna will be hurt."
Kazusa is right. I found that out the painful way due to what happened in Strasbourg.
If Setsuna finds out, she'll undoubtedly be hurt. Then what if we keep it a secret until the very end?
"It's okay, Haruki. You don't need to pretend that you're fine. You don't have to force yourself to act virtuous."
Kazusa says that it's for the sake of everyone.
But does that mean I can keep it hidden? …Can I bear to keep it hidden?
"I'm satisfied having seen her from a distance. I feel great having heard Setsuna sing."
"Kazusa…"
"I couldn't talk to her, and I couldn't even apologize to her, but I can feel a resolve within me now despite that."
I can't tell if the words she's speaking with her shaky voice are optimistic or pessimistic, making me feel even more uncertain…
"Say, Haruki… Do you remember what I said about Setsuna when I joined the Light Music Club?"
"Kind of."
"She'll either become my worst enemy… or the greatest friend of my life."
"In the end, we couldn't become friends… but that was my fault."
Speaking those same words she spoke in the past, she looks up at the same Tokyo, and the same night sky as she did back then.
"That's why right now… I merely don't want to become her enemy. I absolutely can't become that."
Unlike her bitter smile of agreement back then, she shows nothing but a bitter, resigned breakdown in resolve.
"I think that Setsuna… still thinks of you as a friend, Kazusa."
"Stop it, stop it… If you say any more, it won't be just Setsuna who'll suffer, but me too."
"Haruki… Find happiness with Setsuna, okay? Reconcile with her quickly."
The intent of those words, unlike that time, do not make me happy.
"I'm sure Setsuna is already over it. I'm sure she'll forgive you before the day is over."
Kazusa is most likely picking the most correct choice out of those available.
"So when you reconcile, don't ever let go of her again, okay? Ah, just… when you're bringing her to your apartment, give me a call, alright? That way I can leave my apartment for the night."
"Stop messing around…"
"And also, swear to me… Don't ever tell her that I live next to you."
But the truth often carries with it words that can be hard to accept emotionally.
"The two of us, we only live next to each other because of work. And we have a duty of confidentiality about that job. You have a duty to protect my privacy, Haruki."
The times people scorn me or get angry at me are, after all, when I make them feel like this.
"So you can remain employed, Haruki; so you can remain as Mr. Kitahara of the editing department of Kaiousha, you can't tell Setsuna anything about me."
And right now, Kazusa's words reflect my own usual behavior right back at me.
"…It's okay, I'll leave once the concert next week ends. Try to endure it until then, Haruki."
Who's the one trying to endure things? Who's the one trying to hold back?
"That's why, that's why…"
Right now, you're just like me when I try to sound smart.
You're just like me when I'm confident about defeating someone in an argument.
You're just like me when I can't justify my actions using emotions, so I have to resort to cold reasoning.
That's why I know the weakness of that strategy. I know how the opponent feels when they use it.
The only thing I don't know is how to go about defeating that weakness. About how to win against someone employing that strategy.
…That means I'm also aware that I definitely can't win.
"…Sorry."
Because of those thoughts whirling around my head…
I hadn't noticed that Kazusa buried her face into my chest at some point.
"Before you make up with Setsuna… allow me this, just once."
"Kazu…sa."
Kazusa's hair wavers in front of my eyes… The very hair I bound myself.
Even though we spent so much time in the same room, we never found ourselves in this position.
The moment she swore to never do this again, Kazusa decided to break that oath one final time.
1. Hug her.
2. Lend her my chest.
"Kazusa…"
If Kazusa has decided to take back her own statement if even for a moment, I have no reason to hesitate.
…At the very least, not now.
"Y-You can't… You can't, Haruki."
Kazusa trembles in fear on my chest.
She's confused about the arms wrapped around her back, and the cheek pressed against her head.
"Do you have any idea what you're doing? You… and Setsuna… You have Setsuna…"
"Just this once."
Because Kazusa destroyed her own reasoning with her own actions.
And I finally got my chance to counterattack.
Just once. Only for this moment.
"…Don't tell her. Don't you ever tell Setsuna about this."
That's why when Kazusa's own hands wrap around my back, I accept them as a given.
Just like that night of our graduation.
Just like that night when we shared our feelings, and committed our single greatest mistake.
"Haruki… Haruki… Uu-uu… uah…!"
"Mhm…"
Until Kazusa stops crying. Until I return to reality.
"I'm sorry… I'm really sorry."
"Why are you apologizing?"
Kazusa's voice, along with her breath, directly spreads across my chest.
I can't push her away. I can't embrace her either.
I'm the one who wants to apologize, so hearing Kazusa apologize is nothing but sorrowful.
"Only five more minutes… no, only three. Don't move. Don't look at me… Don't ask anything."
"Okay…"
"Thank you, Haruki…"
It's painful knowing the great value Kazusa finds even in my current helplessness.
"Haruki… Haruki… Uu-uu… uah…!"
That's why…
All I did was add ten minutes to the promised time limit…
Until Kazusa finally noticed that the time limit was past and quickly let go of me, I didn't move an inch.
"This is where you were, Setsuna…"
"Yeah…"
"Is everyone outside now?"
"Yes…"
"Let's hurry. You'll be late for the celebration party."
"Tomo…"
"Hm? What is it?"
"Thank you… for dragging me onto the stage again."
"Nothing to be thanked for. It's just a hobby of mine."
"You're usually pretty annoying, but this time I'll be grateful… That's just how fun it was."
"If you could foster some ambition because of this, I'd have nothing more to say."
"Hehe… I told you that's impossible. I'm just an amateur who likes singing."
"Well, let's talk about that at the celebration party. Kei-chan seemed pretty worked up about making you a permanent member this time."
"Let's go, Setsuna. Everyone is waiting for you."
"Hmm, I'm sorry, but I'll pass tonight."
"It's late so I'll go home. Say sorry to everyone for me."
"Why? You have the day off tomorrow, right? You could at least show your face…"
"I've always been a little sheltered. You know that my family is really strict about curfews, don't you?"
"I had fun. I'll be glad to participate if the chance arises again… Can you tell them that?"
"Setsuna…"
"Well then, good work…"
"You're planning on going to Kitahara-san's place, aren't you?"
"You won't hear from your parents about curfew there. All you need to do is to give them a call that you're staying the night."
"…Stop it already. It's proper manners to not say things like that even if you're right."
"But he lied to you, didn't he? You said you'd distance yourself from him for a while."
"Yes, you're right… I did distance myself from him for a while."
"Nothing is resolved yet, and you're going to forgive him…?"
"It's not about forgiving or not forgiving… I'm just unable to hold back any longer."
"Setsuna…"
"Aa-ah, I'm hopeless after all. I simply love him too much."
"When I stood on the stage singing my heart out, I forgot about everything. When I got off the stage, I remembered everything and found my determination to meet him."
"I plan on crying my heart out when I see him… Just kidding, it'll be fake tears. Just a farce to make him realize that he's done something wrong."
"But even if it's fake in the beginning, I'll remember so many things along the way that I'll probably end up crying for real."
"If that happens, we'll be able to confront each other for real. If he forgives me, I'll be able to forgive him… I believe I have that courage right now."
"Setsuna… that's…"
"It's so embarrassing already… Look at what you're making me say, Tomo."
"That's… that's…!"
"Now then… I'll be going, Tomo."
"…! You can't, you can't, Setsuna!"
"Tomo…?"
"You can't right now… You absolutely can't go to where he is!"
"What's the matter? There's no reason to get so upset… Well then, I'll go apologize to everyone now."
"I told you, you can't… he's… Kitahara is an unbelievable traitor!"
